howto_md:
## How to use this booklet

This booklet is a map of the world's cooking. Every entry tells you, in one or two lines, what a cuisine, ingredient, technique or dish is, where it began and why it matters. Every entry has an ID (such as COK-11.3 for dum cooking) that is also its address on the website.

- **Parts** are the big branches (cuisines, taste, ingredients, techniques, dishes, registers, history, people, ideas, health...).
- **Sections (COK-01, COK-02...)** are the main topics; many open with a *Before you start* box.
- **Sub-sections and entries** carry a ☐ box: tick it when you have cooked, tasted or explored it.
- **Registers** give 30 dish cards, a year-wise food timeline, the great awards and guides (checked 13 November 2026), GI foods and a festival food calendar.
- **Tags** (#rajasthani #tadka #jain) and **See also** links connect related pages.
- Start with **Part 0**, six two-minute questions about fire, chilli, bread, umami and memory.
- Recipes are described, never copied from books.

howto_boxes: **Parts:** the intro questions, the master map, cuisines, taste, ingredients, techniques, dishes, registers, history, people, ideas, health, the practical guide, reviews, navigation and sources.
**Sub-sections and entries (☐):** one or two lines each; tick the box when you have cooked or tasted.
**Registers:** 30 dish cards, the timeline, awards and guides, GI foods and festivals. They are a sourced selection; the full lists grow on the website.
**Step 2.** Find your own state's cuisine in Part 2.
**Step 3.** Cook the beginner's 20 dishes in Part 12.
**Step 4.** Follow tags and See also links to gardening, films and books.
**Step 5.** Tick ☐ as you cook, and keep a cooking diary.

Knowledge belongs to the people who created it. Every fact here stands on a source listed in Part 15, and every "latest" fact says when it was checked. Where something could not be verified, we say so instead of guessing. Found a mistake? Tell us, and we will fix it and thank you.
